newsitem.title: USA: Brazil ready to negotiate tax treaty with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Brazil ready to negotiate tax treaty with U.S..

text.p: Brazil is ready to negotiate a treaty with the United States to avoid double taxation, Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said on Tuesday.

Malan told a news conference on the fringes of the World Bank/Interrnational Monetary Fund spring meeting that he had written to U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin to inform him about Brazil's willingness to discuss a tax treaty.
Washington and Brasilia have had such an agreement on their agenda for decades but have never successfully negotiated one.
Malan acknowledged that the difficulties would not hinge on the rates of taxation but rather on congressional ratification of the eventual agreement by both countries.
Many of the past obstacles for reciprocity on tax credits were cleared when Brazil reduced its corporate tax rates to levels similar to those in the United States, he said.
Congressional ratification, on the other hand, was still as hard to predict in Brasilia as in Washington, he argued.

"Some concerns have been addressed to us, to the effect of what would be the Brazilian parliament's decision on this," Malan said. "My answer is a very simple one: could the U.S. executive branch assure anyone about a decision on Capitol Hill? Probably not"
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso does not have an outright majority in the Brazilian Congress while President Clinton's Democrats are in the minority in both houses of the U.S. Congress.
